comparator.name: Human Geography and Planning
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026-2027 Faculty of Spatial Sciences TER defines one 180-EC programme with a fixed 60-EC first year, a 60-EC second year containing one 5-EC restricted elective, and a 60-EC third year containing 30 EC of genuine elective, minor, exchange or internship space. Healthy Ageing is instantiated by the neutral official-order tie-break because it appears first in the TER list of four equally weighted restricted electives; no UCR-fit consideration enters that choice. The two-part Bachelor's Project is represented once at its combined 15 EC. The 30-EC third-year choice space remains open rather than being filled with invented subjects.

components.name: Reflecting on Human Geography and Planning

components.note: First-listed option selected by neutral official-order tie-break from Healthy Ageing, Population and Development, Real Estate Principles, and North America: A Regional Perspective.

components.name: Electives / Minor / Exchange / Internship
components.note: Genuine approved choice space preserved without inventing a student selection.

components.note: The TER schedules 5 EC in semester 2a and 10 EC in semester 2b; represented once at the combined credit load.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme integrates the target's social-spatial, planning, environmental and mixed-method core. Urban governance and globalisation/migration are separately evidenced by direct target interests and produce materially different curricula. All three are mechanically feasible and pairwise differ by at least nine courses, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: Groningen provides a continuous disciplinary sequence in human geography and planning, including dedicated GIS, population and rural geography, fieldwork, planning theory and dynamics, and a bachelor thesis. UCR can combine strong sociology, politics, economics, sustainability, environmental science, data and research courses, but the fixed Fall 2026 catalogue does not offer the same full geography-and-planning sequence. The UCR alternatives therefore cover related subjects and methods without claiming professional planning equivalence.
